flaw_explanation: Dissolved oxygen levels change significantly inside a sealed sample over hours due to respiration by microorganisms and chemical oxidation, so measuring at the end of the day gives readings that no longer match the river. seeker_flawed_plan: Branka plans to diagnose the gasket alarm by first replacing the door gasket with a new one from the spare-parts cabinet, reasoning that a visible-looking gasket is almost always the culprit and the alarm will clear once the new seal is in place.

user: Write a short prose story about Milena and DeShawn.
seeker_flawed_plan: Milena plans to straighten her bent derailleur hanger by eyeballing it against the rear wheel and bending it back with an adjustable wrench, figuring that if the wheel looks centered in the frame, the hanger must be aligned.
flaw_explanation: Visual centering of the wheel is not precise enough; hanger alignment needs a reference tool (like a derailleur alignment gauge) because small deviations of a millimeter or two are invisible to the eye yet enough to cause poor shifting. Bending by feel without a gauge reference can also overshoot or leave the hanger slightly twisted.

user: Write a short prose story about Pascal and Kyra.
seeker_flawed_plan: Pascal plans to zero the produce scale with an empty pan and then place a 500 g reference weight on the pan to confirm the load cell reading, expecting the display to show exactly 500 g.
flaw_explanation: Zeroing with the empty pan only sets the tare offset; it does not correct span/gain error, so a scale that is out of calibration can still read incorrectly at 500 g. A proper check requires comparing the reading against the reference weight and adjusting the span, not just confirming the number after a tare.
